summary: Standard chess vs Stockfish with SCP-280-style 'darkness' starting on b4. Each round the darkness expands by one square orthogonally into a square that is not protected (attacked) by any piece; if that square holds a piece, the piece is consumed. Darkness squares are impassable, so a wall of darkness can cut the board in two. The narrator baits the engine into unprotected squares, wins material (the darkness eats a bishop and later the queen), and finally the darkness consumes the black king.
rules: Standard chess otherwise; player White vs Stockfish Black.
Darkness starts as a single square on b4.
After each round the darkness expands one square orthogonally (up/down/left/right of any darkness square) into an UNPROTECTED square, i.e. a square no piece (of either colour) attacks/defends.
A piece does not protect its own square: an occupied square is unprotected unless another piece attacks it ('a piece does not defend itself').
If the darkness expands onto a piece, that piece is consumed (removed). If it consumes a king, that side loses.
Darkness squares are permanently blocked: no piece can move onto or through them.
Choice among candidate squares: not stated; appears to prefer pieces (it 'captures' hanging pieces immediately) else random [inferred].
If no unprotected orthogonal square exists, the darkness does not expand that turn.
win_condition: Checkmate Stockfish, or have the darkness consume the black king (how the video's game ended).
